declaration: void __thiscall EditorAnimWorld_SetTargetPosition_0059cf00(cEditorAnimWorld *this, int creatureID, Vector3 position, bool applyNow, bool ignoreZ);

stack_arguments.name: position
stack_arguments.type: Vector3 (12 bytes, by value, occupies three argument slots)

mechanics: Spill argument 1 and check the map gate this+0x38; a zero gate returns without any map call.
lower_bound against this+0x0c through a valid local cursor out pointer, then find, then TEST ECX,ECX on the mapped controller: a null controller is an additional early return.
On success load applyNow from [ESP+0x20] and ignoreZ from [ESP+0x24], then LEA EDX,[ESP+0x1c] to take the address of the by-value Vector3 argument on the caller's stack frame.

Forward to 0x0059b0f0 as (controller, &position, applyNow, ignoreZ); the target reads through that pointer, so the callee must keep forwarding the address of its own incoming argument rather than a copy it mutates.
body.abi_note: The Vector3 argument spans three stack slots, so the total callee cleanup is 0x18 rather than 0x10. Forwarding uses the address of the incoming argument block, which is what makes the by-value semantics observable in the target.

evidence.observation: Listing proves the 0x38 gate, the null-controller exit, the [ESP+0x20]/[ESP+0x24] loads, the LEA EDX,[ESP+0x1c] position pointer and the RET 0x18 epilogue.
The forwarded target copies position->x/y/z into controller+0x20 and controller+0x2c before the magnitude clamp, fixing the read-through-pointer contract.

evidence: 0x00e5c780 stores the found node through [ESP+0x8] and dereferences [ESP+0xc] as the search key, so the native stack order after the receiver is (out, key). The port declaration and both call sites use (map, out, key) with a non-null out pointer and the cursor is read back from that slot.

the forwarded pointer differs from the caller's own variable, proving the by-value contract
the lower-bound port receives a non-null out pointer on the hit path
key past the last node forwards nothing
this+0x38 == 0 skips the lookup and the forward
